close_reason: Landed in commit 3ed6aaf. BlobUploadResponse.sha256 is now Option<jmap_cid_types::Sha256> with #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]. Field placement chosen per the bead's recommendation (a): on jmap-base-client's BlobUploadResponse since the spec text is chat-agnostic. Derived Serialize on the struct to support the round-trip preservation tests. The previous uppercase-hex tolerance is lost; that inter-op question is tracked at bd:JMAP-noz7. Four new tests cover typed deserialize, None-elision on serialize, no-sha256 round-trip, and strict rejection of uppercase hex.
description:
Spec: draft-atwood-jmap-cid-00 §3 (Blob upload extension).

Spec text: "Server advertising the CID capability MUST store the blob exactly as received and MUST compute sha256 from those bytes. The Blob/upload response MUST carry the sha256 field of type Sha256."

Current state: Blob upload response in jmap-base-client (likely in src/blob.rs or methods/blob.rs of jmap-chat-client) has no typed sha256 field. The value round-trips through extras today.

## Acceptance

- Add `sha256: Option<jmap_cid_types::Sha256>` field to the BlobUploadResponse type (location TBD by reading jmap-base-client; might be in jmap-chat-client/src/methods/blob.rs — check both)
- The field uses #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]
- Option because servers not advertising the CID capability won't send it
- If the field already serializes via extras with key "sha256", the typed-field promotion replaces the entry; verify no double-serialize
- jmap-cid-types already re-exports Sha256 at the crate root (landed in JMAP-v9py.12 — `pub use digest::{Sha256, Sha256DigestError, Sha256DigestErrorKind};` in lib.rs)
- jmap-base-client adds path-dep on jmap-cid-types (workspace member)
- Test: deserialize a sample Blob/upload response with {"sha256": "deadbeef..." (64 chars)} → sha256 field is Some(_) carrying the parsed digest
- Test: serialize a BlobUploadResponse with sha256: None → no "sha256" key in output
- Test: round-trip preservation — if a server sends {"sha256": null} (legacy), it parses as None and serializes back as nothing (skip_if)

## Open question (file as bead if can't resolve in-band)

Should the field live on:
(a) jmap-base-client's BlobUploadResponse — covers Blob/upload uniformly
(b) jmap-chat-client's blob types — chat-specific

Recommendation: (a). The spec says "Blob upload response" without chat-coupling; jmap-base-client is the right home. Confirm by reading jmap-base-client/src/blob.rs (or whichever module has the upload type) before opening the edit.

## Out of scope

- Computing sha256 (deployment's job)
- Cross-blob dedup countermeasures (spec leaves this server-discretion)
- FileNode sha256 (separate; would be a Layer D.5 if we add filenode integration — currently out of scope per "3 crates + CID" decision)
title: Layer D: Wire sha256 typed field into Blob upload response (jmap-base-client)
